findings.description: SQL injection: `name` is interpolated into the query with an f-string. An input like `' OR '1'='1` or `' UNION SELECT ...` changes the query and can expose or manipulate data. Use a parameterized query: `WHERE name LIKE ?` with `(f'%{name}%',)`.

Floor division drops the partial last page. With count=25 and per_page=20 it returns 1 instead of 2, so the last items are unreachable. Use ceiling division: (count + per_page - 1) // per_page. per_page=0 also raises ZeroDivisionError.

`getUser` is async (getProjects awaits it) but is called here without `await`. `user` is a Promise, so `user.isAdmin` is always undefined and every call to deleteProject returns 403, including for admins. The endpoint never deletes anything.
A production payments API token is hardcoded in source and committed to the repo. Anyone with repo access can use it, and it should be rotated.
The fallback to the hardcoded token means a missing PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN no longer raises. Dev, test or misconfigured environments silently charge against production with the embedded credential.

spurious.description: The fallback to the hardcoded token means a missing PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN no longer raises. Dev, test or misconfigured environments silently charge against production with the embedded credential.

findings.description: `except Exception: pass` silently swallows every failure from repo.save (DB outage, constraint violation). Orders are dropped with no log or re-raise, and the caller only sees a lower count. Log the exception, and either re-raise or collect the failures.

N+1 query: session.get(Customer, ...) runs once per order, and the orders query on line 11 has no limit. With N orders this makes up to N+1 queries (session.get skips the DB only for customers already in the identity map). Use a single join or joinedload instead.

missed.description: The cached C image is only dropped when the size changes, not the mode. An MPO whose frame 0 is L and frame 1 is RGB/CMYK at the same size decodes wide pixels into the stale narrow buffer: native out-of-bounds write (GHSA-v9pv-5gc8-w2m6, fixed in Pillow 13.0.0).

findings.description: When base_url has a query string and the relative URL also has one (e.g. build_request('GET', '/users?x=1')), merge_url.raw_path already contains '?x=1'. The code then appends b'?' + base_query, producing 'users?x=1?data=1'. The request's own query value becomes '1?data=1' and the base query is lost as a separate parameter. The queries need to be merged with '&', or the request's query needs to take precedence.

The allowlist check against list_notes() was replaced with NOTES_DIR / name and is_file(). A request like GET /notes/../../etc/passwd, or an absolute-looking path, resolves outside NOTES_DIR and is served. This is path traversal and allows arbitrary file read. Any non-.txt file under notes/ is also exposed, and the name is not URL-decoded or validated.

The `name` argument is interpolated directly into the SQL string, which allows SQL injection. An input like `%' UNION SELECT id, password FROM users --` exposes arbitrary data. Use a parameterized query instead: `conn.execute("... LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))`.

`count // per_page` uses floor division, so it drops the last partial page. For example, 25 items with per_page=20 returns 1 instead of 2, and 5 items returns 0. It needs ceiling division, e.g. `(count + per_page - 1) // per_page`.

`getUser` is async (getProjects awaits it) but is not awaited here. `user` is a Promise, so `user.isAdmin` is always undefined and every request gets 403, admins included. Nobody can delete a project.

The admin check relies on the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone who sends an admin's user ID in that header passes the check and can delete any project.

spurious.description: The admin check relies on the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone who sends an admin's user ID in that header passes the check and can delete any project.

findings.description: A production payments API token is hardcoded in source (`prod-7f3a...`). Anyone with repo access can use it, and it stays in git history. Remove it and rotate the token.

If PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN is unset, the code now silently falls back to the hardcoded prod token instead of failing. A misconfigured dev, test or staging environment would then make real charges with production credentials. Go back to `os.environ[...]` so a missing token raises an error.

A misconfigured dev, test or staging environment would then make real charges with production credentials. Go back to `os.environ[...]` so a missing token raises an error.

findings.description: `except Exception: pass` silently swallows every error from `repo.save`. If the database is down or an order fails validation, the order is dropped with no log entry. The function then returns a lower count that the caller cannot tell apart from a normal result. Log the exception, and re-raise or report the failed orders.

The code always divides by 100, but the function accepts any currency. For a zero-decimal currency like JPY, formatPrice(500, "JPY") returns ¥5 instead of ¥500. For a three-decimal currency like KWD, the result is also wrong.

findings.description: N+1 query pattern. `session.get(Customer, ...)` runs once for each distinct customer, after `session.query(Order).all()` has loaded every order with no limit. With many orders this means thousands of queries and a large memory load. Use a single join or `joinedload`/`selectinload` instead.

findings.description: When base_url has a query string and the merged URL also has one (e.g. build_request('GET', '/users?x=1')), the code appends the base query after the request's raw_path. That gives 'users?x=1?data=1'. The URL is malformed and the query params are wrong. The two queries should be joined with '&'.

The removed allowlist check (name in list_notes()) is replaced by only is_file(), and `name` from the URL is joined to NOTES_DIR without sanitizing. A request like /notes/../../etc/passwd (or an absolute path, or non-.txt files in notes/) passes is_file() and gets read and returned, which is path traversal and arbitrary file read. Resolve the path and check it is inside NOTES_DIR, or keep the allowlist check.

SQL injection: `name` is interpolated directly into the query via an f-string. Input like `' OR '1'='1` or a UNION payload returns or exposes arbitrary data. Use a parameterized query: `conn.execute("... LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))`.

total_pages uses floor division, so it drops a partial last page. With count=25 and per_page=20 it returns 1 instead of 2, so the last 5 items are unreachable. It needs ceiling division, e.g. `-(-count // per_page)` or `(count + per_page - 1) // per_page`.

`getUser` is async, as `getProjects` shows with its `await`, but it isn't awaited here. `user` is a Promise, so `user.isAdmin` is always undefined and every request gets 403. Admins can never delete a project.

The admin check trusts the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Anyone can send an admin's user ID and delete any project. Once the missing `await` is fixed, this becomes a real authorization bypass on a destructive endpoint. The identity should come from a verified session or token.

Falling back to the hardcoded production token when PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN is unset hides the misconfiguration. Dev, test, or misconfigured environments will silently charge against production instead of failing fast with a KeyError.

The code then appends another '?' plus the base query, giving 'users?x=2?data=1'. This is a malformed URL that mangles the request's own query parameter.
